newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen hit new highs on Nikkei's collapse.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen hit new highs on Nikkei's collapse.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen futures surged to new contract highs on Friday as the Tokyo stock market's biggest one-day drop in two years buoyed confidence the Bank of Japan would maintain its low interest rate regime.
Dealers said Euroyen futures rose in the afternoon after the 225-share Nikkei average plunged through the floor to end 770.22 points or 4.26 percent lower at 17,303.65.
The lead September Euroyen contract was at 99.34 at 1125 GMT after hitting a new high of 99.35 against an IMM close at 99.29.
But the dealer with the Japanese institution said Japanese investors were more likely to sell off their holdings of U.S. treasuries first.
"They can make money both ways by selling U.S. treasuries -- on the yield and on the exchange rate," he said.
Eurodollar futures finished little changed ahead of the U.S. non-farm payrolls data for December, due at 1330 GMT on Friday.

"All the estimates show expectations of quite an increase so it would take an extremely strong number, something above 200,000, to make them come off further," said the trader with the U.S. futures house.

"I would tend to be a seller anywhere above 99.35. September's another eight months from now," said a trader with a Japanese institution, noting that this was too far ahead to bet on continued low rates in Japan.
Japanese government bond futures for March ended at 125.52 against their previous 124.84.
A trader with a U.S. house said continued weakness in Tokyo stocks could induce investors to liquidate other Japanese assets, such as bonds, to cover their losses.
June Eurodollars ended at 94.23 against an IMM close at 94.22.
